main_text.p: AlFirauzabadius, Safioddinus, &c. الكعبات AlCaabat, domum etiam quam Banu Rabia circumire olim religionis ergo solebant. Jam vero de Lapide nigro quid non fabulantur? eum è pretiosis Paradisi lapidibus cum Adamo in terram demissum, ac postea diluvii tempore rursus in cœlum sublatum, vel alibi, (حمدن شا الله) i.e. tibi Deo visum est, ut loquitur Ahmed Josephi filius, in monte Abu Kobais, ut Zamachsharius in Alcorani c. 2. reposition, ac demum aedificanti templum Abrahamo ab Angelo Gabriele reportatum. esse eum (يمين الله) {*} i.e. dextram Dei in terris. Situs est in angulo Caabæ Eraciensi, illo scil. qui Basram respicit, cubitis binis & 1/3, a terra remotus, juxta Safioddinum, vel quod eodem recidit (سبعة اشبار) i.e. Septem Spithamarum distantia, juxta Shahaboddinum Authorem libri, (مسالك الابصار) &c. quem tamen, tam Deo charum (ut autumant) tam Arabibus ac Mohammedanis omnibus sacrum {†}Karmatiani anno Hejræ 317. juxta AbulFedam & Ahmedem Josephi filium, (quo anno obiit celeberrimus Astro-
Rendering of Arabic script in the margin and text is uncertain; see notes.

* Vulgo [illegible, ~4 letters] a. tegniusnomus * AlBattanius,) vel 319 juxta Sajioddinum, lo-co motum abstulerunt,nec ante annum 339. (morte Philosophorum inter Arabes facilè principis, Al-Farabii celebrem) ut iterum AbulFeda & Ahmed Ebn Tusef, vel 335. ut Sajioddinus, ab ipsis vel prece vel pretio impetrari potuit ut remitterent: idque لما ادعى عن تحويل الحجاج عليهم[?] i.e. cum vi-derent nullo modo fieri posse, ut peregrini ad ipsos à Mecca diverterent, ut ait Ahmed Ebn Tusef,qui me-rito asserit fuisse hoc مصيبة ما اصاب الاسلام بمثلها[?] i.e.

page.notes: Margin notes, top to bottom: "Algazali, Shi-haboddin, & Amad Ebn Yusef." (left, beside "ra remotus"); "* Exemplaria nonnulla pro se ferre videntur" (left, mark *); an Arabic word with "i." and "oculus Dei, & sed mendose." (left, no mark); "† Nomen Sethæ." (left, mark †). The Arabic words in the text and in the margin are uncertain and were not read letter by letter; the parenthetical Arabic in the body (after "(", "esse eum", "Septem", "&c.") should be checked against the scan. The Arabic in the margin note is best-effort. The asterisk in the text ("* i.e. dextram") is a reference mark, written as {*}. The Greek/Arabic rendering "reportatum" and "reposition" should be checked: "reposition" is possibly "repositum" in print. The printed page continues below the cut; the paragraph ends mid-word ("Astro-") and carries on onto the next part. The Arabic phrases are copied from the scan and are uncertain in their letters, so they are marked [?]. The left marginal note is partly covered by a dark blot; only "* Vulgo", "a." and "tegnius" can be read.
